MLOps - Deploy ML workload to K8S

Jan 20, 2025

ML Project Lifecycle in the Real World

So far the local ML practice is just the beginning, in a real world production environment, ML projects typically follow a structured lifecycle and often deployed in scalable, cloud-based environments. Cloud Providers like AWS with Managed Kubernetes Services (EKS) to provides orchestration, scaling, and fault tolerance to handle ML workloads.

Path for delpoying MLOps workload in K8S

  • Transition from local ML practice to a K8S-based deployment (This post)
  • Start with MLOps tools like Kubeflow.
  • Shift from local to cloud platforms (AWS) to deploy ML workload on EKS.
  • Practice deploying models using REST APIs (local) and APT Gateway (AWS).
  • Try local data engineering (ETL pipelines, data lakes, etc.), then move to AWS data service and solution for ML workload.

Setting up Minikube with GPU on WSL Ubuntu

  • First let’s create a Minikube cluster with GPU support on WSL Ubuntu. This will be the local K8S environment for testing and deploying ML workloads.
  • Nest step, once the K8S is ready, let’s run a GPU pod to test if a K8S pod can access GPU.
  • Now let’s create a more complex GPU workload that trains a simple CNN on MNIST dataset, with a ResourceQuota and LimitRange to allocate the GPU in minikube, we will use the tensorflow/tensorflow:2.14.0-gpu to better support CUDA and NVIDIA drivers to complete the training job.
  • Deploy the MNIST Training and resource quota into minikube

What we’ve achieved

So here we are able to set up a Minikube with local GPU support, integrated NVIDIA GPU (RTX 3070 Ti), by validating CUDA with TensorFlow GPU integration, deploy a CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) training on MNIST with final test accuracy: 98.99%.

In next post I will explore how to manage Kubeflow for more complex machine learning senarios and enable Prometheus and Grafana for ML workload monitoring.
